items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-09-01
items.q: The only brass bass player that I can think of that was playing inside then in those days was a guy called Lefty Ironman, who played with Buck Banville at the Plum Plant, the American Legion Dance Hall.

ctx.x: No, they didn't seem to be in style in those days. It was a piano bass drums rhythm section. That was the fad. Now black bands used banjo players. I believe Papa Celestan, Papa Celestan's band played for my senior prom. And he had a banjo in his band. But it was a string bass too. It wasn't a tuba.

The only brass bass player that I can think of that was playing inside then in those days was a guy called Lefty Ironman, who played with Buck Banville at the Plum Plant, the American Legion Dance Hall. That may have been a place you didn't go to.
Now Cink Martin played an iron bass on occasion. He was a good bass player too. Good tuba player. Cink Martin. But not often.
